newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Twelve Ethiopian plane survivors return to Addis.
newsitem.headline: Twelve Ethiopian plane survivors return to Addis.

text.p: Twelve of the 50 survivors from the Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 disaster flew back to Addis Ababa from the Comoro islands on Thursday.

Ethiopian Airlines stewardesses, wearing black in mourning for the dead, welcomed the two surviving stewardesses with hugs and kisses. Friends and relatives of the other two Ethiopians wept tears of joy to see them alive again.

The other eight were four Nigerians, an Indian, a Malian, a Malawian and a Djiboutian. Ethiopian Airlines is arranging for them to fly on, except for Joalune Mokone, third secretary at the Malawian embassy to Ethiopia, who left for her Addis Ababa home.
But the families of 22 Ethiopians killed in the incident were stilling waiting on Thursday for the bodies to come home.
Altogether 125 people were killed when the plane crashed on Saturday into the sea off the Comoro islands. The plane was hijacked en route to Nairobi and apparently ran out of fuel.

The airline said it had a plane on standby to fly to the Comoros to collect the bodies of the crash victims. "We are waiting for a word from the crash site. Until then we have to be patient," an airline official said. The airline said on Wednesday that it had recovered all the 125 bodies.
